name: e03_parameter_robustness
title: 3. Parameter robustness: is 50/200 a plateau or a lucky spike?
text:
**Question.** Is EMA50/200 a robust choice on a plateau of similar rules, or a lucky cell that does not survive the grid search?

**Setup.** 62 EMA crossovers (fast 5-150, slow 50-400) on SPY, QQQ and BTC, default settings, one common window per asset after the slowest EMA warms up (1996 / 2002 / 2017 to 2026). Nulls: "Sharpe over T-bills = 0" and "mean return minus buy-and-hold's = 0" (PSR/DSR, CSCV PBO with S = 16); a paired stationary bootstrap compares 50/200's Sharpe with buy-and-hold's. The common window starts later than the full histories of sections 2 and 9, because it waits for the 400-bar EMA (SPY from 1996-09-24 instead of 1994-11-28, QQQ from 2002-11-08 instead of 2001-01-05), so 50/200's Sharpe here differs from theirs: SPY 0.53 vs 0.59, QQQ 0.71 vs 0.69; QQQ's window excludes the 2001-02 decline.

**Findings.**

- 50/200 Sharpe: SPY 0.53 (rank 44, above B&H 0.48, grid IQR 0.53-0.57); QQQ 0.71 (rank 10, level with B&H 0.71, grid IQR 0.63-0.70); BTC 1.00 (rank 32, above B&H 0.97, grid IQR 0.94-1.10), of 62. Each IQR is 8%-15% of the median and only 0.22-0.47 of one standard error of a Sharpe estimate (0.18 / 0.20 / 0.32): a plateau. BTC tilts towards short slow windows (slow <= 150: 1.11; >= 250: 0.95). 50/200 differs from its four neighbours' average by -0.03 / +0.05 / +0.03 (at most 0.23 s.e.): neither a spike nor a hole.
- 90% / 18% / 61% of cells beat B&H on Sharpe, but 10% / 0% / 0% earn a higher mean return (50/200 IR -0.13 / -0.23 / -0.25). 50/200's Sharpe gain over B&H is +0.05 [-0.19, +0.32] / +0.00 [-0.23, +0.26] / +0.02 [-0.35, +0.41] (95% CI). None of the three gains is distinguishable from zero.
- Absolute null: the best cells (EMA100/300, EMA40/150, EMA20/75) have DSR 0.998 / 0.998 / 0.999, but B&H's own PSR is 0.996 / 1.000 / 0.999: the test only says the assets went up. Relative null: the deflated P(best-IR cell beats B&H) is 0.22 / 0.03 / 0.21; for 50/200 with no search (N = 1) it is 0.23 / 0.13 / 0.22.
- PBO: 76% / 79% / 48%. Across CSCV splits the in-sample winner's Sharpe falls from 0.70 / 0.81 / 1.31 to 0.50 / 0.61 / 1.00 out of sample, at or below the grid median.
- README BTC story (2017-2026): EMA12/128 Sharpe 1.11 (above 87% of the grid), EMA50/200 1.00 (above 48%), so the "improvement" reverses. Both IRs vs B&H are negative (-0.19, -0.25); 12/128 still compounds to more (8557% vs 7605%) through lower volatility drag, not a higher average return. Counting two tries, P(50/200 beats B&H) is 0.18.

**Interpretation.** Crossovers of any length are weighted sums of past returns (Levine & Pedersen 2016), so every cell makes the same bet; the first principal component explains 79%-85% of the correlation of their active returns, so N = 62 overstates the independent trials and the DSR haircut is conservative. The sharpest local peak is the cell a search would report, QQQ's EMA40/150 (0.74 vs neighbours 0.67). PBO above 50% means the in-sample winner usually lands *below* the median rule out of sample; among near-ties this is partly mechanical, because CSCV halves are complements (Bailey et al. 2017). Either way, the ranking of cells is noise. Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014) and Harvey & Liu (2015) explain why the bar must rise with the number of trials; even "N = 1" flatters 50/200, which became textbook by looking good on decades of US equity data (collective data snooping; Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999), while QQQ and BTC were chosen as famous winners. The absolute claim (trend timing earns more than T-bills) survives any reasonable N, but "earns more than buy-and-hold" fails even at N = 1. Moving from 12/128 to 50/200 is a step between noisy points on one surface, not skill.
after: PBO and DSR answer different questions: DSR asks whether the *selected* Sharpe is too high to be the best of N lucky draws; PBO asks whether the *selection procedure* (pick the in-sample best) tends to pick an out-of-sample loser. A flat plateau can pass the first and fail the second: when all configurations are near-ties, ranking them is noise.
